definition_zh: 神秘的；难以解释的；讳莫如深的
definition_en: strange and difficult to explain; having a hidden or supernatural quality; deliberately keeping things unclear
core_image: 一扇只开一条缝的门，缝里透出一点看不清的光
scene: 村口的老宅多年无人居住，夜里楼上的窗子却总亮着。The old house keeps a mysterious light burning in its upper window.
sceneCN: 这里是「神秘的、难以解释的」（第 1 个义项：来路不明、说不清楚）；句意为那座老宅楼上窗里始终亮着一盏莫名的灯。图中可辨识物件：老宅、亮着的窗、夜色。

pos.zh: 神秘的；难以解释的；讳莫如深的

derivatives.zh: 由 mysterious 加 -ly 构成，义为「神秘地」
由 mysterious 加 -ness 构成，义为「神秘性」
与 mysterious 同出希腊语词根，义为「谜；神秘事物」

senses.title: Strange and hard to explain
senses.definition: difficult to understand or explain because the facts are hidden
senses.definitionCN: 因事实被遮蔽而难以理解或解释
senses.example: The old house keeps a mysterious light burning in its upper window.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老宅楼上窗里始终亮着一盏莫名的灯。
senses.why: Greek myein meant to close the lips or the eyes, so the family of words starts from what is shut away from view and only later describes how such a thing feels.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 myein 意为闭口或闭眼，因此这一族词的起点是「被关在视线之外的东西」，之后才用来形容这种东西给人的感觉。

senses.title: Touching on hidden or supernatural power
senses.titleCN: 带有神秘力量的；玄秘的
senses.definition: having a quality that seems to come from a hidden or supernatural source
senses.definitionCN: 带有似乎来自隐秘或超自然来源的性质
senses.example: The valley was said to hold mysterious forces that spoiled milk overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 据说那条山谷里有神秘的力量，能让牛奶一夜之间变坏。
senses.why: The word first named secret religious rites open only to the initiated; that closed door of ritual left it with a permanent air of the beyond.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指名只有入会者才能参加的秘仪；仪式那扇关着的门，让它永久带上了一层超验的气息。

senses.title: Deliberately unclear about something
senses.titleCN: 讳莫如深的；故意不说清
senses.definition: choosing to keep one's actions or intentions vague on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意把自己的行为或意图说得含糊
senses.example: She was mysterious about where the money had come from.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这笔钱的来路讳莫如深。
senses.why: Anyone who refuses to explain looks, from outside, exactly like a thing that cannot be explained, so the adjective moves from the unknown object to the person hiding it.
senses.whyCN: 一个人拒绝解释，从外面看就和一件无法解释的东西一模一样，于是这个形容词从被未知的对象转到了藏起它的人身上。

intro.en: Mysterious comes through French from Latin, where the noun had already travelled from Greek rites closed to outsiders.
intro.cn: mysterious 经法语来自拉丁语，而拉丁语中那个名词早已从「不许外人参与的希腊仪式」一路传来。

items.en: The verb myein meant to close, especially the eyes or the lips, and it gave the family its sense of shutting away.
items.cn: 动词 myein 意为闭合，尤指闭眼或闭嘴，为这一族词提供了「关起来、不示人」的意思。

items.en: A mysterion was a secret rite or doctrine revealed only to those admitted to it.
items.cn: mysterion 指只向获准入会者揭示的秘密仪式或教义。

items.en: Latin took the word as mysterium, keeping both the ritual sense and the broader sense of a secret.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个词写作 mysterium，既保留仪式义，也泛指秘密。

items.en: French formed the adjective mysterieux from the same stem, and it carried the sense of something unexplained rather than something sacred.
items.cn: 法语用同一词干造出形容词 mysterieux，词义已偏向「说不清的事」，不再限于神圣之事。

items.en: English adopted the French adjective, respelled it with ous, and extended it to people who refuse to explain themselves.
items.cn: 英语借入这个法语形容词，改写成带 ous 的形式，并把词义扩展到「不肯解释自己的人」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun, the adverb and other words on the same Greek stem; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for what cannot be explained.
note.cn: 形近组收同出希腊词根的名词、副词及其他同族词；近义组收表示「无法解释」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for something unexplained or kept secret.
entries.definitionCN: 表示无法解释或被人保密之事的名称。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a way that cannot be explained.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为「神秘地、莫名其妙地」。

entries.definition: The quality of being strange and unexplained.
entries.definitionCN: 神秘、难以解释的性质。

entries.definition: To puzzle someone completely, from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 使人完全困惑，同出这一词干。

entries.definition: A person who seeks direct union with the divine.
entries.definitionCN: 追求与神直接合一的人；神秘的。

entries.definition: Unusual and hard to account for, but without the hint of hidden meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 不寻常、难以说明，但没有「背后另有隐情」的暗示。

entries.definition: Hard to understand because the pieces do not fit.
entries.definitionCN: 因线索拼不起来而令人费解。

entries.definition: Deliberately or naturally hard to read, like a riddle.
entries.definitionCN: 像谜语一样难以看透，可指有意为之。

entries.definition: Simply not yet accounted for, without any aura.
entries.definitionCN: 只是尚未得到解释，不带神秘气氛。

normalIntro.en: The word is the adjective of a Greek noun for closed rites, and its relatives still circle around secrets.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是希腊语中表示秘仪的名词的形容词形式，它的同族词至今仍围绕「秘密」打转。

normal.en: Greek myein meant to close the eyes or lips, so mysterious begins with the image of a mouth kept shut.
normal.cn: 希腊语 myein 意为闭上眼或闭上嘴，所以 mysterious 的起点是一张闭紧的嘴。

normal.en: Mystery is the noun and mysterious the adjective; adding ous turns a secret into a quality.
normal.cn: mystery 是名词，mysterious 是形容词；加上 ous，就把一个秘密变成了一种性质。

normal.en: The ending is said quickly as -əs, which is why the last syllable almost disappears in speech.
normal.cn: 词尾读得很轻，接近 -əs，所以最后一个音节在口语里几乎听不见。

normal.en: Mystify is the verb of the same family: to make someone feel they are facing a closed door.
normal.cn: mystify 是同一族的动词：让人觉得自己面对的是一扇关着的门。

normal.en: Mysterious circumstances and a mysterious smile both keep the facts just out of reach.
normal.cn: mysterious circumstances 与 a mysterious smile 都让事实停在伸手够不到的地方。

abstract.en: A door left ajar is more disturbing than a door locked tight, because the gap promises something behind it.
abstract.cn: 虚掩的门比紧锁的门更让人不安，因为那道缝许诺了门后有东西。

abstract.en: Every closed rite and every unopened letter teaches the same lesson about hidden knowledge.
abstract.cn: 每一场闭门仪式、每一封未拆的信，都在讲同一件关于隐秘知识的事。

abstract.en: A word that began with shut lips ends by describing the face of someone who will not answer.
abstract.cn: 一个从「闭紧嘴唇」开始的词，最后用来形容一张不肯回答的脸。

examples.en: A mysterious figure was seen near the gate last night.
examples.cn: 昨夜有人在门附近看见一个神秘的身影。

examples.en: The case remains mysterious after thirty years.
examples.cn: 三十年后这桩案子依然扑朔迷离。

examples.en: He gave a mysterious smile and changed the subject.
examples.cn: 他神秘地笑了笑，换了话题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密斯特瑞斯」——把秘密密起来，脸上就带出神秘；mysterious 就是神秘的。

root: 希腊语 myein（闭口、闭眼）构成 mysterion（秘仪），经拉丁语 mysterium 与法语 mysterieux 进入英语；一般认为词根与「闭合」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what is shut away from view; the senses spread from unexplained events to sacred hidden power and to people who hide their own reasons.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被关在视线之外」；义项从无法解释的事件，扩展到隐秘的神圣力量，再转到有意藏起自己理由的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door opened only a crack, with a light inside that cannot be made out.
core.cn: 核心意象：只开一道缝的门，里面有看不清的光。

branches.en: a lamp left burning in an empty house
branches.cn: 空屋里一直亮着的灯

branches.en: a footprint that stops halfway across a room
branches.cn: 走到房间中间就断掉的脚印

branches.en: a rite held behind a curtain
branches.cn: 帘子后面举行的仪式

branches.en: milk souring overnight in a valley
branches.cn: 山谷里一夜变坏的牛奶

branches.en: an answer that slides away from the question
branches.cn: 绕开问题的回答

intro.en: The word is built from a Greek verb of closing, its noun of secret rites, a Latin borrowing, and an English adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语表「闭合」的动词、其表示秘仪的名词、拉丁语的借形，以及一个英语形容词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek noun as mysterium and formed mysticus from the same root, and both stand behind the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语名词借作 mysterium，又用同一词根造出 mysticus，两者都支撑着英语这一族词。

definition_zh: 谜；神秘事物；神秘气氛；悬疑作品
definition_en: something that cannot be explained or is kept secret; the quality of being secret; a story built around an unsolved puzzle
core_image: 一只上锁的抽屉，里面的东西不翼而飞，锁却完好无损
scene: 书房的抽屉少了一封信，锁面没有撬痕，窗子也从里面扣着。The letter vanished from a locked drawer, and the mystery is still unsolved.
sceneCN: 这里是「谜、无法解释的事」（第 1 个义项：找不到答案的事件）；句意为信从上锁的抽屉里消失，这个谜至今未解。图中可辨识物件：抽屉、锁、信、窗扣。

pos.zh: 谜；神秘事物；神秘气氛；悬疑作品

derivatives.zh: 由 mystery 的词干加 -ous 构成，义为「神秘的」
由 mysterious 加 -ly 构成，义为「神秘地」
由同一词干加 -ify 构成，义为「使困惑不解」

senses.title: Something that cannot be explained
senses.definition: a fact or event that resists explanation and keeps people guessing
senses.definitionCN: 无法解释、让人不断猜测的事实或事件
senses.example: The letter vanished from a locked drawer, and the mystery is still unsolved.
senses.exampleCN: 信从上锁的抽屉里消失，这个谜至今未解。
senses.why: The Greek noun named rites closed to outsiders; once the ritual frame fell away, what remained was a fact shut off from explanation, which is the everyday sense today.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊名词本指不许外人参加的仪式；仪式的外壳脱落之后，剩下的就是一个被挡在解释之外的事实，也就是今天的日常义。

senses.title: The quality of being secret or strange
senses.definition: an atmosphere of secrecy that surrounds a person, place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 笼罩在人、地点或事物周围的神秘气息
senses.example: An air of mystery hangs over the house at the end of the lane.
senses.exampleCN: 巷子尽头那座房子笼罩着一层神秘气息。
senses.why: Because the word names what is withheld, it can also name the withheld quality itself, so a place becomes mysterious by carrying a mystery rather than by containing one.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词指被扣住不说的东西，它也能指那种被扣住的性质本身，于是一个地方不必真的藏着什么谜，只要带着谜的气息就显得神秘。

senses.title: A story built around a puzzle
senses.definition: a book, film or play whose plot turns on an unexplained event and its solution
senses.definitionCN: 以未解事件及其解答为主线的小说、电影或戏剧
senses.example: She reads a murder mystery every week before bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周睡前读一本谋杀悬疑小说。
senses.why: Readers wanted the pleasure of a puzzle that gets solved, so the word moved from the puzzle itself to the kind of book that delivers one.
senses.whyCN: 读者想要的是「谜被解开」的快感，于是这个词从谜本身转到了提供这种谜的那类书。

intro.en: Mystery reached English through Old French from Latin, and the Latin noun had already borrowed a Greek word for rites open only to the initiated.
intro.cn: mystery 经古法语、拉丁语进入英语，而拉丁语名词此前已借入一个希腊词，指只许入会者参加的仪式。

items.en: The verb myein meant to close, especially the lips or the eyes, and the sense of shutting away runs through the whole family.
items.cn: 动词 myein 意为闭合，尤指闭嘴或闭眼，这一族词始终带着「关起来」的意思。

items.en: A mysterion was a secret rite or teaching that insiders guarded from outsiders.
items.cn: mysterion 指内部人对外人守口如瓶的秘密仪式或教义。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as mysterium, where the sense widened from a rite to any hidden matter.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 mysterium，词义从仪式扩大到任何隐秘之事。

items.en: Old French mistere carried both the religious sense and the sense of a hidden truth, and passed the word to English.
items.cn: 古法语 mistere 兼有宗教义与「隐秘真相」义，并把这个词传入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the puzzle sense, adds the atmosphere sense and the name of a literary genre.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「谜」义，又添上「气氛」义，并把词用作一类文学体裁的名称。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjective, the verb and other relatives on the same stem; the near-meaning group holds words for puzzles and secrets.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形容词、动词及其他同族词；近义组收表示谜题与秘密的词。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a name for closed rites and now covers any unexplained fact, the feeling around it, and the books written about it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是闭门仪式的名称，如今覆盖任何无法解释的事实、围绕它的感觉，以及以此为题材的书。

normal.en: The word goes back to Greek myein, to close the lips; a mystery is something someone keeps their mouth shut about.
normal.cn: 这个词可追到希腊语 myein（闭嘴）；mystery 就是有人闭口不谈的事。

normal.en: The plural is mysteries, with y changing to ies, the same pattern as story and stories.
normal.cn: 复数是 mysteries，y 变 ies，与 story、stories 的变化方式相同。

normal.en: Mystery is the noun, mysterious the adjective, mystify the verb; the family keeps one stem and changes only the ending.
normal.cn: mystery 是名词，mysterious 是形容词，mystify 是动词；这一族共用同一词干，只换词尾。

normal.en: An air of mystery needs no hidden fact; it can be produced by a closed door and a dim lamp.
normal.cn: an air of mystery 并不需要真藏着什么；一扇关着的门和一盏昏暗的灯就能造出它。

normal.en: A murder mystery is a genre label, so the word can name a shelf in a bookshop as well as a puzzle in a locked room.
normal.cn: a murder mystery 是体裁标签，所以这个词既能指密室里的谜，也能指书店里的一个书架。

abstract.en: A locked drawer with nothing missing teaches that a question can outlast its answer.
abstract.cn: 一只什么都没丢的上锁抽屉，说明问题可以比答案活得更久。

abstract.en: Every secret is a room whose door is shut from the inside, and every mystery is the light under that door.
abstract.cn: 每个秘密都是从里面关上的房间，而每个谜都是门缝下透出的光。

abstract.en: A word that names a closed rite ends up naming the pleasure of watching a lock be picked.
abstract.cn: 一个命名闭门仪式的词，最后用来命名「看别人开锁」的乐趣。

examples.en: The cause of the fire remains a mystery.
examples.cn: 起火的原因仍然是个谜。

examples.en: He enjoys solving mysteries set in old hotels.
examples.cn: 他喜欢破解以老旅馆为背景的谜案。

examples.en: Her sudden departure is shrouded in mystery.
examples.cn: 她的突然离开笼罩在神秘之中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密斯特瑞」——秘密被锁在密室里，就成了谜；mystery 就是谜。

root: 希腊语 myein（闭口、闭眼）派生的 mysterion（秘仪）经拉丁语 mysterium、古法语 mistere 进入英语；一般认为核心是「对外人闭合」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a fact kept behind a closed door; the senses extend to the atmosphere such a fact creates and to stories built on solving it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被关在门后的事实；义项扩展到这种事实造成的气氛，以及以解开它为骨架的故事。

senses.title: The word by which a person or thing is known
senses.definition: the word or set of words used to identify a person, animal, place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用来指认某人、某动物、某地或某物的词或词组
senses.example: She wrote her name at the top of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 她把名字写在了页面顶端。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the spoken label that calls a person over; every other sense in the word grows out of that act of naming.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是喊人时用的那个称呼；这个词的其他义项都从「叫名字」这个动作长出来。

senses.title: The reputation attached to a person or group
senses.definition: the opinion that other people have of a person, company or product, built up over time
senses.definitionCN: 他人对某人、某公司或某产品长期形成的看法
senses.example: The old bakery still has a good name in this neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老面包店在这一带仍然名声很好。
senses.why: A name stands for a person, so it can also stand for how that person is judged; the label becomes the reputation hanging on it.
senses.whyCN: 名字代表一个人，因此也能代表别人对他的评价；这个标签就变成了挂在它上面的名声。

senses.title: To give a name to someone or something
senses.definition: to give a name to a person, animal, place or thing, especially at the start of its life or use
senses.definitionCN: 给某人、某动物、某地或某物取名字，尤指在生命或使用的开端
senses.example: They named the boat after the captain's daughter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以船长的女儿为这条船命名。
senses.why: The noun supplies the label and the verb supplies the act of putting that label on a new thing, so a baby, a boat and a street can all be named.
senses.whyCN: 名词提供标签，动词提供「把标签贴到新事物上」的动作，所以婴儿、船只和街道都可以被命名。

senses.title: To appoint or specify someone
senses.definition: to officially choose someone for a position, or to state exactly which person or thing is meant
senses.definitionCN: 正式选定某人担任某职，或明确指出所指的是哪个人或哪件东西
senses.example: The board named her as the new director.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会任命她为新任主管。
senses.why: A name singles one person out of a crowd, so the verb can mean picking that person and putting them into a post, with the authority of the speaker behind it.
senses.whyCN: 名字把一个人从人群里单独点出来，所以这个动词可以指把那个人挑出来放到某个职位上，背后是说话者的权力在起作用。

intro.en: Name goes back to an old word for the spoken label, and its senses have spread from that label to reputation and to the act of appointing.
intro.cn: name 可追溯到表示「口头称呼」的古词，义项从这一称呼扩展到名声，再扩展到任命这一动作。

items.en: A reconstructed noun for name is widely accepted, and the same root lies behind Latin nomen and Greek onoma.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个表示「名字」的原始印欧语名词，同一个词根也见于拉丁语 nomen 与希腊语 onoma。

items.en: The reconstructed form namô meant name, and it is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.cn: 重构形式 namô 意为名字，是英语这个词的直接祖先。

items.en: Old English nama was the everyday noun for a name, and it also supplied the verb namian, to name.
items.cn: 古英语 nama 是表示名字的日常名词，并派生出动词 namian，意为命名。

items.en: Middle English kept name as a noun and namen as a verb, and the spelling settled into its modern shape.
items.cn: 中古英语保留名词 name 与动词 namen，拼写逐渐固定为现代形式。

items.en: Modern English extends the noun to reputation and the verb to official appointment, as in naming a new director.
items.cn: 现代英语把名词扩展到名声，把动词扩展到正式任命，如 naming a new director。

note.cn: 形近组收这个词自己的词族，以及几个只是押韵的拼写；近义组收表示标签、头衔与名声的词。

entries.definition: Having no name, or too ordinary or bad to be described by one.
entries.definitionCN: 没有名字的，或平凡、恶劣得无法用名字描述的。

entries.definition: Existing in name only, or relating to a name; from the Latin nomen.
entries.definitionCN: 仅名义上存在的，或与名字有关的；出自拉丁语 nomen。

entries.definition: The state of being known by many people; it rhymes with name but has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 被很多人知晓的状态；与 name 押韵，但词源不同。

entries.definition: The word attached to a book, film or person as a mark of rank.
entries.definitionCN: 附在书籍、影片或人身上、表示等级或名称的词。

entries.definition: A small piece of paper or a short word that says what something is.
entries.definitionCN: 说明某物是什么的小纸片或简短词语。

entries.definition: The general belief that people hold about someone's character or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 人们对某人品格或品质普遍持有的看法。

entries.definition: To choose someone officially for a purpose or post.
entries.definitionCN: 正式选定某人担任某职或用于某目的。

normalIntro.en: The word is the plain noun for a spoken label, and all its senses are different ways of using that label.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是表示「口头称呼」的朴素名词，所有义项都是使用这一称呼的不同方式。

normal.en: Old English nama is the direct ancestor, and the modern spelling keeps the same four letters at the start.
normal.cn: 古英语 nama 是直接祖先，现代拼写开头仍保留同样的四个字母。

normal.en: Namely is name plus -ly, and it introduces the exact name of the thing just mentioned.
normal.cn: namely 是 name 加 -ly，用来引出前面那件事的确切名字。

normal.en: Nameless is name plus -less, so it describes someone with no name or no distinct identity.
normal.cn: nameless 是 name 加 -less，用来形容没有名字或没有鲜明身份的人。

normal.en: Nomen is the Latin word for name, and it gives English nominal, nominate and nomination.
normal.cn: nomen 是拉丁语中的「名字」，由此有了英语的 nominal、nominate、nomination。

normal.en: In the name of is a fixed phrase in which name stands for the authority behind an act.
normal.cn: in the name of 是固定说法，这里的 name 代表一个行为背后的权力。

abstract.en: A name is a sound that makes one thing stand out from everything else, so the word is always about singling out.
abstract.cn: 名字是一种让某物从其他一切中站出来的声音，所以这个词始终关乎「单独点出」。

abstract.en: Because a name travels without the person, it can carry praise or blame long after the person is gone.
abstract.cn: 名字可以脱离本人四处流传，所以人不在场之后，它仍能承载赞誉或责备。

abstract.en: To be named to a post is to be pointed at in public, which is why the verb can mean both calling and choosing.
abstract.cn: 被任命到一个职位，就是在众人面前被点到，所以这个动词既能指称呼，也能指挑选。

examples.en: She wrote her name at the top of the page.
examples.cn: 她把名字写在了页面顶端。

examples.en: They named the boat after the captain's daughter.
examples.cn: 他们以船长的女儿为这条船命名。

examples.en: The old bakery still has a good name in this neighbourhood.
examples.cn: 那家老面包店在这一带仍然名声很好。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a spoken label; the senses then divide into the label itself, the reputation it carries, the act of giving it, and the act of pointing to a chosen person.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个口头称呼；义项分出称呼本身、它承载的名声、给它命名的动作，以及把选定之人点出来的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden board is carved with one word and hung up, and from then on the thing has an identity people can call.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块木牌刻上一个字、挂了起来，从此这件东西就有了可被人呼唤的身份。

branches.cn: 店门上方一块木牌上刻着一个词

latinIntro.en: Latin nomen is generally treated as a cognate of name through the same older root, and it is the source of the learned words nominal and nominate.

definition_zh: 自然的；天然的；天生的；正常的
definition_en: existing in nature rather than made by people; also inborn, and normal or expected
core_image: 一株野草从石缝里自己钻出来，没有人去栽种
scene: 山脚下有一片从未开垦的林地，藤蔓顺着倒下的树干自己爬上去。The reserve protects the natural habitat of the local birds.
sceneCN: 这里 natural 是「自然的、天然的」（第 1 个义项：非人造）；句意为保护区守护当地鸟类的天然栖息地。图中可辨识物件：倒木、藤蔓、林地。

pos.zh: 自然的；天然的；天生的；正常的

senses.title: Existing in nature, not made by people
senses.definition: found in nature and produced without human making or control
senses.definitionCN: 存在于自然界、并非由人制造或控制而产生的
senses.example: The park protects the natural habitat of the birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这座公园保护着鸟类的天然栖息地。
senses.why: The Latin noun natura names the way things are born and grow, so natural starts from what comes into being without human hands.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 natura 指事物出生、生长的样子，所以 natural 的起点是未经人手而生成的东西。

senses.title: Inborn rather than learned
senses.definition: present in a person or animal from birth and not learned
senses.definitionCN: 人与生俱来、并非后天学到的
senses.example: She has a natural gift for languages.
senses.exampleCN: 她天生就有语言天赋。
senses.why: If natura is the way something is born, a quality that arrives at birth is literally natural, which is why talent can be natural.
senses.whyCN: 既然 natura 指事物出生时的样子，出生就带来的特质自然就是「天生的」，天赋也就能说成 natural。

senses.title: Normal and to be expected
senses.definition: what normally happens and therefore does not surprise anyone
senses.definitionCN: 按常理会发生，因此不令人意外
senses.example: It is natural to feel nervous before a test.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前感到紧张是正常的。
senses.why: What follows nature follows a regular course, so natural extends from how things grow to how things usually happen.
senses.whyCN: 顺着本性发展的东西有其常规，于是 natural 从「事物如何生长」扩展到「事情通常如何发生」。

senses.title: Relaxed and not put on
senses.definition: used of behaviour or manner that is easy and sincere, with no pretending
senses.definitionCN: 形容举止轻松真诚，不装样子
senses.example: His smile was warm and natural.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笑容温暖而自然。
senses.why: A person who behaves as nature made them, without forcing a pose, looks natural, which gives the word its social sense.
senses.whyCN: 一个人按本性行事、不硬摆姿势，看上去就是 natural，这就是这个词的社交义。

intro.en: Natural comes from the Latin noun natura, which itself grows out of nasci, to be born.
intro.cn: natural 来自拉丁名词 natura，而 natura 又由 nasci（出生）生长出来。

items.en: Nasci meant to be born, the root behind nature, native and innate.
items.cn: nasci 意为出生，是 nature、native、innate 共同的根。

items.en: Natura named the character or course of things, what a thing is born to be.
items.cn: natura 指事物的本性或进程，即事物生来就该有的样子。

items.en: Naturalis meant belonging to nature or coming from birth.
items.cn: naturalis 意为属于自然的，或与生俱来的。

items.en: Old French naturel passed into Middle English natural, keeping both the world sense and the inborn sense.
items.cn: 古法语 naturel 进入中古英语作 natural，同时保留「自然界」和「天生」两义。

items.en: Modern English adds the meanings normal and unaffected, which grow from the idea of following nature.
items.cn: 现代英语又添「正常」与「不做作」两义，都由「顺其自然」的想法长出。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the same birth stem; the near-meaning group collects words for what is normal and inborn.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「出生」词干上的词；近义组收表示正常与天生的词。

entries.definition: The physical world and the character built into a thing.

entries.definition: Present in a person from birth, not learned.

entries.definition: What is usual and expected, with nothing odd about it.

entries.definition: Existing in a person from birth rather than gained later.
entries.definitionCN: 与生俱来而非后天获得的。

entries.definition: Grown or produced without artificial chemicals or processes.
entries.definitionCN: 不使用人工化学物或工艺而生长、生产的。

normal.en: Natura is Latin for the way things are born and grow, so natural is first about the world, not about people.
normal.cn: natura 是拉丁语中事物出生、生长的样子，所以 natural 首先说的是世界，而不是人。

normal.en: Naturally adds -ly, and it doubles as an answer word meaning of course.

senses.title: Close to the place mentioned, before a noun
senses.definition: used before a noun for a place or thing that is only a short distance from the place being talked about
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词之前，指距离所说地点不远的地方或事物
senses.example: A nearby shop was still open, and the children ran in for sweets.
senses.exampleCN: 附近一家小店还开着，孩子们跑进去买糖。
senses.why: Near came from Old English neah, close at hand, and by from Old English bi, beside; putting them together produced a word whose whole job is to sit in front of a place and shorten the distance.
senses.whyCN: near 来自古英语 neah，意为「在手边」；by 来自古英语 bi，意为「在旁边」；两者合起来，造出一个专门放在地点名词前、把距离缩短的词。

senses.title: At a short distance away, after a verb
senses.definition: used after a verb or at the end of a clause to say that something happens a short distance from the place mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 放在动词之后或句末，表示事情发生在离所说地点不远的地方
senses.example: She lives nearby and walks over most mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 她住在附近，大多数早晨都走过来。
senses.why: English often lets a compound work as an adverb without any ending, so the same two prepositions that named a place beside another place also came to describe where an action happens.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让一个复合词不带词尾就直接作副词，于是原本用来说「在一个地点旁边的另一个地点」的两个介词，也用来描述动作发生在哪里。

intro.en: Nearby is a plain English compound of two Old English words for closeness, and it has been recorded only since the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: nearby 是两个表示「接近」的古英语词合成的普通英语复合词，有记录的历史只能追溯到十八世纪。

items.en: Neah meant close at hand, and its comparative near later became an ordinary adjective for what is not far.
items.cn: neah 意为在手边，它的比较级 near 后来变成普通形容词，表示「不远的」。

items.en: Bi meant beside, near or by the side of, and it survives in by, beside and the second half of nearby.
items.cn: bi 意为在旁边、靠近，它留在 by、beside 以及 nearby 的后半截里。

items.en: Middle English already paired near with by in phrases about standing or living close to a place.
items.cn: 中古英语已在表示「站在或住在某处近旁」的短语里把 near 与 by 配在一起。

items.en: The written compound nearby appears in the eighteenth century, first in American usage, and spreads in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 写成一个词的 nearby 在十八世纪出现，最早见于美国用法，十九世纪渐渐流行。

items.en: Modern English uses it both before nouns and after verbs, so one form covers two grammatical jobs.
items.cn: 现代英语让它既用于名词之前，也用于动词之后，同一个形式承担两种语法角色。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the two words that were joined to make the compound plus their derived forms; the near-meaning group holds adjectives and adverbs of closeness.
note.cn: 形近组收合成这个复合词的两个来源词及其派生形式；近义组收表示「接近」的形容词与副词。

entries.definition: Not far away, as a preposition, adjective or adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 不远的；作介词、形容词或副词。

entries.definition: Almost, but not quite; built on the same root with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎但不完全；同一词根加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being close in space or time.
entries.definitionCN: 空间或时间上接近的状态。

entries.definition: The superlative of near, for the shortest distance of all.
entries.definitionCN: near 的最高级，表示距离最短。

entries.definition: Only a small distance away, often with a stronger sense of contact.
entries.definitionCN: 距离很小，常带「贴近」的意味。

entries.definition: Lying next to something, usually sharing a border.
entries.definitionCN: 紧挨着某物，通常指相邻接壤。

entries.definition: Situated next to or in the same district as something else.
entries.definitionCN: 位于某物旁边或同一区域的。

entries.definition: In the area on every side of a place, without naming one spot.
entries.definitionCN: 在某地四周的范围内，不指某一处。

normalIntro.en: The word is simply near plus by, two old English words for closeness that fused into one adjective and adverb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 near 加 by，两个表示「接近」的古英语词合并成一个形容词兼副词。

normal.en: Old English neah meant close at hand, and by came from bi, beside; nearby is those two ideas welded together.
normal.cn: 古英语 neah 意为在手边，by 来自 bi（在旁边）；nearby 就是这两个意思焊在一起。

normal.en: The compound is written as one word, unlike the phrase near by, which still appears in older texts.
normal.cn: 这个复合词写成一个词，与旧文献里仍能见到的短语 near by 不同。

normal.en: Before a noun it is an adjective: a nearby town; after a verb it is an adverb: she lives nearby.
normal.cn: 放在名词前是形容词：a nearby town；放在动词后是副词：she lives nearby。

normal.en: Nearly looks like the same word with -ly, but it means almost, not at a short distance.
normal.cn: nearly 看起来只是加了 -ly，意思却是「几乎」，而不是「在不远处」。

normal.en: Nearness is the noun made with -ness, useful when the sentence needs a subject rather than a place.
normal.cn: nearness 是用 -ness 构成的名词，句子需要一个主语而不是地点时就用它。

abstract.en: Two short words for standing beside something can do the work of a whole phrase about distance.
abstract.cn: 两个表示「站在旁边」的短词，就能顶替一整句关于距离的描述。

abstract.en: A word that only shortens distance shows how much English trusts a compound to do a preposition's job.
abstract.cn: 一个只负责缩短距离的词，说明英语多么信任复合词去承担介词的工作。

abstract.en: What is nearby is not yet reached, which is why the word always leaves a small gap open.
abstract.cn: 「附近的」东西还没有被走到，所以这个词总留着一小段没走完的距离。

examples.en: Several nearby farms lost power in the storm.
examples.cn: 附近几座农场在风暴中停了电。

examples.en: The hotel is convenient for nearby restaurants.
examples.cn: 这家旅馆去附近的餐馆很方便。

examples.en: My parents live nearby, so we see them often.
examples.cn: 我父母住在附近，所以我们常去看他们。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼尔拜」——抬脚就到旁边那条街，说一声就到了；nearby 就是附近的。

root: 古英语 neah（近）与 bi（在旁）复合，十八世纪出现 nearby；属日耳曼语词，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place at a short distance; the same form then splits by grammar into an adjective in front of nouns and an adverb after verbs.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「距离不远的一处地方」；同一个形式随后按语法分工，成了名词前的形容词和动词后的副词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two garden walls separated by a narrow lane, each house able to see the other's lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：两户院墙之间只隔一条窄巷，各家都能看见对方窗里的灯。

branches.en: a shop two doors down the lane
branches.cn: 隔两个门面的那家小店

branches.en: a village within walking distance
branches.cn: 走几步就到的村子

branches.en: a lane where both walls can see one lamp
branches.cn: 两面墙都看得见同一盏灯的窄巷

branches.en: a neighbour walking over with a bowl
branches.cn: 端着一只碗走过来的邻居

branches.en: a short walk taken most mornings
branches.cn: 大多数早晨都要走的一小段路

intro.en: The word is built from an Old English adjective of closeness, an Old English preposition of position, and the English endings that grew around them.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语中表示「接近」的形容词、表示位置的介词，以及围着它们长出的英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Near and by are Germanic words, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for the compound.
latinIntro.cn: near 与 by 都是日耳曼语词，这个复合词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 几乎；差不多；将近；密切地
definition_en: not quite, but very close to being true or to happening; also used before amounts to mean a little less than the figure
core_image: 车门在眼前缓缓合上，脚尖离踏板只差半步
scene: 雨刚停，站台上的人陆续散去，广播已经在报最后一班车。I nearly missed the last train because the lift was slow.
sceneCN: 这里是「几乎、差一点」（第 1 个义项：接近但未达到）；句意为电梯太慢，我差一点错过末班车。图中可辨识物件：站台、广播、湿地面、车门。

pos.zh: 几乎；差不多；将近；密切地

derivatives.zh: nearly 的词根，义为「近的；接近的」
由 near 加 -ness 构成，义为「接近；临近」，与 nearly 同族

senses.title: Almost, but not completely
senses.definition: not quite true or not quite done, though very close to it
senses.definitionCN: 非常接近，但还没有完全达到或完成
senses.example: I nearly missed the last train because the lift was slow.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯太慢，我差一点错过末班车。
senses.why: Near began as a word for physical closeness, and the ending -ly first meant in a close manner; spoken English then stretched that short gap from space into degree, so a thing that is close to happening becomes nearly happening.
senses.whyCN: near 原本表示空间上的接近，词尾 -ly 最初意为「以接近的方式」；口语把这个小缝隙从空间拉到位次，于是「接近发生」的事就成了「几乎发生」。

senses.title: Very close to a stated amount or time
senses.titleCN: 将近；差不多（数量或时间）
senses.definition: used before figures and periods to say that the real amount is a little below the one named
senses.definitionCN: 放在数字与时间段之前，表示实际数量略低于所说的那个数
senses.example: Nearly a thousand people came to the opening.
senses.exampleCN: 将近一千人参加了开幕式。
senses.why: Measuring a short distance and measuring a small shortfall use the same picture, so the word that once said two places are close now says a total is close to a round figure.
senses.whyCN: 量一小段距离与量一小点差额用的是同一幅画面，于是那个原本说「两地相近」的词，现在说「总数接近某个整数」。

senses.title: Closely, in family connections
senses.titleCN: 密切地；亲近地（指亲属关系）
senses.definition: used with related or connected to mean closely, chiefly in older or careful English
senses.definitionCN: 与 related 等词连用表示「关系密切」，多见于较旧或较正式的英语
senses.example: The two families were nearly related by marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个家庭因婚姻而关系很近。
senses.why: The older sense of the adverb was simply closely, and kinship is where that sense survives; the everyday sense moved away to almost, leaving this use behind like a fossil.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词较早的意思就是「紧密地」，亲属关系正是这层意思的留存处；日常义漂向「几乎」，把这一用法像化石一样留在了原地。

intro.en: Nearly is near plus the old adverb ending, and its meaning drifted from closely to almost while one formal use kept the older sense.
intro.cn: nearly 是 near 加旧副词词尾，词义从「紧密地」漂到「几乎」，只有一种正式用法保留了旧义。

items.en: Neah meant close at hand, and its comparative gave English the form near that nearly is built on.
items.cn: neah 意为在手边，它的比较级给英语提供了 near 这个形式，nearly 就建在它上面。

items.en: The ending -lice meant in the manner of, and it is the ancestor of the modern -ly in nearly and other adverbs.
items.cn: -lice 意为「以……的方式」，是现代副词词尾 -ly 的前身，nearly 等词都用它。

items.en: Middle English ner meant both near and closely, and the new adverb nerliche carried the sense of closely, carefully.
items.cn: 中古英语 ner 兼有「近」与「紧密」两义，新的副词 nerliche 表示「紧密地、仔细地」。

items.en: The adverb is recorded in the sixteenth century; by the seventeenth the sense almost is common in speech and in print.
items.cn: 这个副词在十六世纪见于记录；到十七世纪，「几乎」义已在口语与书面语中常见。

items.en: Modern English keeps almost as the main sense, adds the counting use before numbers, and retains closely only in phrases about kinship.
items.cn: 现代英语以「几乎」为主义，又添上数字前的计量用法，只在与亲属关系有关的短语里保留「密切地」。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the root and the forms built directly on it; the near-meaning group holds other adverbs that stop just short of a fact.
note.cn: 形近组收词根以及直接建在词根上的形式；近义组收其他表示「差一点、差不多」的副词。

entries.definition: Not far away, in space, time or degree.
entries.definitionCN: 空间、时间或程度上不远的。

entries.definition: The quality of being close, made with -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -ness 构成的「接近、临近」这一性质。

entries.definition: The comparative of near, for a smaller distance.
entries.definitionCN: near 的比较级，表示更近的距离。

entries.definition: The superlative of near, for the smallest distance.
entries.definitionCN: near 的最高级，表示最近的距离。

entries.definition: Very close to, and often interchangeable with nearly before a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 非常接近，在动词前常可与 nearly 互换。

entries.definition: In effect, though not strictly true; stronger in speech than nearly.
entries.definitionCN: 实际上差不多，口语中语气比 nearly 更强。

entries.definition: Almost entirely, used of conditions rather than of counted things.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎完全，多用于状态而非可数之物。

entries.definition: About, allowing for a margin on either side rather than falling short.
entries.definitionCN: 大约，允许上下浮动，而不专指不足。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic root for closeness with an old adverb ending, and its main sense has slid from manner into degree.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语「接近」词根加旧副词词尾，主义从「方式」滑到了「程度」。

normal.en: Near means close, and -ly once meant in that manner, so nearly first described how something was done, not how complete it was.
normal.cn: near 意为近，-ly 原表示「以那种方式」，所以 nearly 最初描述的是做法，而不是完成程度。

normal.en: Before a verb, nearly and almost usually exchange freely: I nearly fell, I almost fell.
normal.cn: 在动词前，nearly 与 almost 通常可以互换：I nearly fell 与 I almost fell 意思相同。

normal.en: Before a number, nearly means a little below it; about or approximately allows the figure to be above as well.
normal.cn: 在数字前，nearly 表示略低于该数；about 或 approximately 则允许高于该数。

normal.en: Not nearly is a fixed phrase of strong denial: the job is not nearly finished means it is far from finished.
normal.cn: not nearly 是语气很强的固定说法：「the job is not nearly finished」意为「离完成还差得远」。

normal.en: Nearly related keeps the old sense of closely, which is why it sounds formal beside the everyday almost.
normal.cn: nearly related 保留了「密切」的旧义，所以它放在日常的 almost 旁边会显得正式。

abstract.en: A closing door measured in half steps shows how English turns a gap in space into a gap in degree.
abstract.cn: 用半步来量的合上的车门，说明英语怎样把空间里的缝隙变成程度上的缝隙。

abstract.en: The same word can fall just short of a train and just short of a thousand, because counting is only measuring with numbers.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以差一点赶上车，也可以差一点到一千，因为计数不过是拿数字来量。

abstract.en: A fossil sense survives in family talk, reminding us that nearly once meant tightly, not almost.
abstract.cn: 一个化石般的旧义活在亲属称谓里，提醒人 nearly 曾经意为「紧紧地」，而不是「几乎」。

examples.en: The bottle is nearly empty; we need another.
examples.cn: 瓶子快空了，我们得再拿一瓶。

examples.en: She has worked here for nearly twenty years.
examples.cn: 她在这里工作了将近二十年。

examples.en: It was nearly midnight when the phone rang.
examples.cn: 电话响的时候已将近午夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼尔利」——差一步就到「near」，可惜还没到；nearly 就是几乎、差一点。

root: 古英语 neah（近）的比较级 near，加副词词尾 -lice（现代 -ly）构成；属日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small remaining gap; it can be a gap before an event, a gap below a number, or the old gap of close kinship.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「剩下的一小段差距」；它可以是事件之前的差距、数字以下的差距，也可以是旧义里亲属之间的贴近。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a train door sliding shut while one foot is still half a step from the step.
core.cn: 核心意象：车门正在合上，一只脚离踏板还差半步。

branches.en: a hand reaching a door as it closes
branches.cn: 车门合上时伸过去的手

branches.en: a platform emptying after the last announcement
branches.cn: 最后一次广播后渐渐空去的站台

branches.en: a hall filled just short of a thousand
branches.cn: 坐得差一点满一千人的大厅

branches.en: a guest list counted twice at a wedding
branches.cn: 婚礼上数了两遍的宾客名单

branches.en: two families joined by one marriage
branches.cn: 因一桩婚姻连在一起的两家人

intro.en: The word is a Germanic adjective of closeness, an Old English adverb ending, and the modern shapes of both.
intro.cn: 这个词由日耳曼语表示「接近」的形容词、一个古英语副词词尾，以及两者在现代的形式构成。

latinIntro.en: Nearly belongs to the Germanic family of near, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: nearly 属于 near 这一日耳曼语词族，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: all but, by a very small margin

definition_zh: 必要的；必需的；必然的；必需品（常用复数 necessaries）
definition_en: needed so that something can be done or achieved; certain to happen as a result; and, as a plural noun, the things a person needs
core_image: 一把钥匙插进锁孔，门后是缺了它就办不成的那件事
scene: 出发前一晚，队长把清单摊在木桌上逐项核对，缺了任何一样队伍都走不成。A map and a compass are necessary for the route they have chosen.
sceneCN: 这里「necessary」是「必要的、必需的」（第 1 个义项：缺了就无法完成某事）；句意是地图和指南针是他们所选路线必需的装备。图中可辨识物件：木桌上的清单、地图、指南针。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 necessitas 进入英语，义为「必要性；必然性；必需品」
由 necessary 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「必然地」
由 necessary 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不必要的」

senses.title: Needed for a purpose
senses.definition: required so that something can happen or be achieved
senses.definitionCN: 为了做成某事而不可缺少的
senses.example: Water is necessary for every living cell.
senses.exampleCN: 水对每个活细胞来说都是必需的。
senses.why: Latin necessarius first meant what cannot be avoided; English moved that force into the practical sphere, where it marks what cannot be left out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 necessarius 最初指躲不开的东西；英语把这份强制感移进日常事务，用来标出不能漏掉的那一项。

senses.title: Certain to follow as a result
senses.definition: certain to happen as a result of something else, with no real alternative
senses.definitionCN: 作为另一件事的结果必定发生，没有别的可能
senses.example: A rise in temperature is a necessary result of the reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 温度上升是这场反应的必然结果。
senses.why: If a thing cannot be avoided, it can also be called necessary as a consequence: the cause leaves the effect no room to differ.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既躲不开，也就可以作为结果被称为必然：原因没给结果留下任何差异的余地。

senses.title: Things a person cannot do without
senses.definition: the items a person needs for daily life, usually used in the plural form
senses.definitionCN: 日常生活离不开的物品，通常用复数形式
senses.example: The family packed only the necessaries for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人只收拾了过冬最基本的必需品。
senses.why: An adjective turns into a noun when English wants to name the objects that carry the quality; the plural marks a set of such objects rather than one.
senses.whyCN: 当英语想直接称呼带有这种性质的物件时，形容词就变成名词；复数标记的是一整套这样的东西，而不是单件。

intro.en: Necessary reached English through French from Latin, and its root idea is not simply wanted but impossible to avoid.
intro.cn: necessary 经法语从拉丁语进入英语，它的根义不是「想要」，而是「避不开」。

items.en: Behind the Latin word lie a negative particle and a root for yielding, though the exact prehistoric form is not settled.
items.cn: 这个拉丁词的背后有一个否定小词和一个表示退让的词根，但更早的确切形式尚无定论。

items.en: Latin necesse meant unavoidable; one widely repeated account divides it into ne, not, and cedere, to give way.
items.cn: 拉丁语 necesse 意为不可避免；一种流传很广的解释把它分成 ne（不）与 cedere（退让）。

items.en: The adjective necessarius described what one cannot do without and passed both necessity and practical need to later languages.
items.cn: 形容词 necessarius 指离不开的东西，把「必然」与「实际需要」一起传给了后世语言。

items.en: Old French necessaire carried the word to England after the Norman conquest, where it was spelled in several ways.
items.cn: 古法语 necessaire 在诺曼征服后把这个词带到英格兰，当时拼写有好几种。

items.en: Modern English uses necessary for what is required and for what must follow, and the plural noun for the bare items of daily life.
items.cn: 现代英语用 necessary 既指「必需」也指「必然」，复数名词则指日常生活里最基本的那些东西。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the same Latin stem and its endings; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what cannot be done without.
note.cn: 形近组沿同一拉丁词干及其词尾展开；近义组收表示「缺了就不行」的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb formed from necessary with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 由 necessary 加 -ly 构成的副词。

entries.definition: The state of being necessary, or a thing that is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 必要性；必需品。

entries.definition: To make something necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事成为必要。

entries.definition: Not needed; more than is required.
entries.definitionCN: 不必要的；多余的。

entries.definition: Absolutely needed for something to exist or work.
entries.definitionCN: 某物存在或运作绝对需要的。

entries.definition: Needed for life or for success.
entries.definitionCN: 生命或成功所必需的。

entries.definition: Demanded by a rule or by the situation.
entries.definitionCN: 规则或情形所要求的。

entries.definition: Too important to be done without.
entries.definitionCN: 重要到不可缺少的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin refusal to yield, put to work in shopping lists, rules and consequences; the family keeps that double life.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是拉丁语里「不肯退让」的劲头，后来被用在清单、规则和结果上，同族词一直保留这双重身份。

normal.en: Necesse carries the sense of what will not give way, which is why necessary can mean both required and certain.
normal.cn: necesse 带着「不肯让步」的意味，所以 necessary 既能指「必需」，也能指「必然」。

normal.en: The plural noun necessaries is old-fashioned but correct for a set of daily needs.
normal.cn: 复数名词 necessaries 虽显旧，但指一整套日常所需时是正确的。

normal.en: Unnecessary adds un-, and the word simply reverses: not needed rather than needed.
normal.cn: unnecessary 加了 un-，词义直接反转：不是必需，而是不必要。

normal.en: Necessity names the state, necessitate the act, and necessary the quality, all from one Latin base.
normal.cn: necessity 指状态，necessitate 指动作，necessary 指性质，三者同出一个拉丁词干。

normal.en: If necessary is a fixed phrase that shortens a whole conditional clause into two words.
normal.cn: if necessary 是固定说法，把一个完整条件句压缩成两个词。

abstract.en: A key that opens one door is necessary only because of that door; the word always implies a purpose behind the need.
abstract.cn: 一把钥匙之所以必需，是因为有那扇门；这个词背后总藏着一个目的。

abstract.en: A necessary result is a consequence with no side road, which is why the same adjective can sound like fate.
abstract.cn: 必然结果是一条没有岔路的结果，所以同一个形容词有时听起来像命运。

abstract.en: Calling things necessaries reduces a whole life to a short list of objects that must be carried.
abstract.cn: 把东西叫作 necessaries，等于把一整段生活压缩成一张必须携带的短清单。

examples.en: The repair is necessary before the bridge can reopen.
examples.cn: 桥要重新开放，先得完成这项维修。

examples.en: Sleep is necessary for the body to recover.
examples.cn: 睡眠对身体恢复是必要的。

examples.en: The shelter kept only the bare necessaries for the night.
examples.cn: 收容所只留了过夜最基本的必需品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呢色塞瑞」——必需品总在「呢色」堆里被翻出来；记住 necessary 是必要的、必然的。

root: 拉丁语 necesse（不可避免）一般认为由 ne-（不）与 cedere（退让）构成，派生形容词 necessarius；经古法语 necessaire 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what cannot be done without; the senses then split into practical need, forced consequence, and the plural noun for the objects themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「缺了就不行」；义项分出实际需要、被迫产生的结果，以及直接指物件本身的复数名词。

core.cn: 核心意象：一把钥匙插进锁孔，没有它就打不开那扇门。

branches.cn: 清单上有一项被圈了两遍

branches.cn: 反应开始后温度计一路上升

branches.cn: 货架上标着日常所需的那一排

intro.en: A Latin negative, a verb of yielding, an adjective and two English endings build this entry from the inside out.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁否定成分、一个表示退让的动词、一个形容词和两个英语词尾，从内到外搭起这个词条。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is well recorded: necesse, its derived adjective necessarius, and the verb cedere that the negative element is thought to contain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基有明确记载：necesse、由它派生的形容词 necessarius，以及一般认为藏在否定成分里的动词 cedere。

definition_zh: 颈；脖子；领口；（瓶、琴等的）细长颈部；地峡；拥吻
definition_en: the part of the body joining the head to the shoulders; a narrow joining part of an object; the opening of a garment; a narrow strip of land; and, informally, to kiss and hold someone closely
core_image: 一双手环绕在头与肩之间，把两端连成一条柔软的通道
scene: 入冬后风从领口灌进来，母亲把围巾绕过孩子颈后，又把垂下来的一端塞进外套。She wrapped the scarf around the child's neck and tucked the loose end into his coat.
sceneCN: 这里「neck」是「脖子、颈部」（第 1 个义项：连接头与肩的身体部位）；句意是母亲把围巾绕在孩子脖子上，把垂下的一端塞进外套。图中可辨识物件：围巾、外套、被风掀起的领口。

pos.zh: 颈；脖子；领口；细长颈部；地峡

derivatives.zh: 由 neck 与 line 复合而成，义为「领口线；领口」
由 neck 与 lace 复合而成，义为「项链」
由 turtle 与 neck 复合而成，义为「高领；高领毛衣」

senses.title: The part joining the head to the body
senses.definition: the narrow part of the body that connects the head to the shoulders and chest
senses.definitionCN: 连接头部与肩胸之间那段较窄的身体部位
senses.example: The cat rubbed its neck against the door frame.
senses.exampleCN: 猫把脖子蹭在门框上。
senses.why: Old English hnecca named the narrow bridge between head and trunk; the shape of a constriction between two wider ends is what the word first points at.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hnecca 指的就是头与躯干之间那条窄窄的桥；这个词最早指向的是「两端宽、中间收窄」的形状。

senses.title: A narrow joining part of an object
senses.definition: the long narrow part of an object, such as a bottle or a stringed instrument, that joins it to the rest
senses.definitionCN: 瓶子、弦乐器等物件上细长的连接部分
senses.example: The label was glued around the neck of the bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 标签被粘在瓶颈上。
senses.why: Any object shaped like that bridge lends its narrow joining part the same name, because the picture is a constriction between two wider ends.
senses.whyCN: 任何物件只要长得像那条桥，它的细长连接处就借用了同一个名字，因为画面仍是「两端宽、中间收」。

senses.title: The opening of a garment
senses.definition: the part of a shirt, dress or sweater that surrounds the neck and is shaped to fit it
senses.definitionCN: 衬衫、连衣裙或毛衣上围着脖子、按颈部形状裁出的开口
senses.example: She pulled the sweater down over a wide neck.
senses.exampleCN: 她把毛衣往下拉，盖住宽大的领口。
senses.why: The garment opening sits exactly where the body's neck passes through, so the word transfers from the body to the cloth that surrounds it.
senses.whyCN: 衣服的开口正好位于脖子穿过的地方，于是这个词从身体转到了包住身体的那层布上。

senses.title: A narrow strip of land between waters
senses.definition: a narrow piece of land that joins two larger areas of land and has water on either side
senses.definitionCN: 连接两片较大陆地、两侧临水的狭长地带
senses.example: The village stood on a low neck of land between two bays.
senses.exampleCN: 村子坐落在两个海湾之间一块低矮的地峡上。
senses.why: A strip of land with water on both sides looks like a narrow joining piece, so the same word is used for an isthmus.
senses.whyCN: 两侧临水的一条陆地，看起来就像一块窄窄的连接件，所以同一个词也被用来指地峡。

senses.title: To kiss and hold someone closely, in informal use
senses.definition: in informal speech, to kiss and caress someone while holding them close
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示搂着某人亲吻、抚摸
senses.example: Two teenagers were necking on a bench by the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 两个少年在湖边的长椅上拥吻。
senses.why: Two people holding each other head to head put their necks close together, and English took the body part as a verb for that embrace.
senses.whyCN: 两个人耳鬓相贴地抱在一起时，脖子挨得最近；英语便拿这个身体部位作动词，指这种拥抱。

intro.en: Neck is a Germanic body word whose deeper origin is uncertain, and it has spread from the body to bottles, clothes and land.
intro.cn: neck 是日耳曼语的身体词，更早的来源不确定；它从身体扩展到瓶子、衣服和土地。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain; some accounts link the Germanic word to a root for bending or pressing together, but this is not settled.
items.cn: 更早的来源不确定；有说法把它与表示「弯曲、压紧」的词根联系起来，但并未定论。

items.en: A reconstructed form such as hnakkaz is generally given for the Germanic word for the back of the neck.
items.cn: 一般认为日耳曼语中表示颈背的词有一个类似 hnakkaz 的重构形式。

items.en: Old English hnecca named the neck or nape, and the initial hn- was still pronounced at that stage.
items.cn: 古英语 hnecca 指颈或颈背，当时词首的 hn- 还要发音。

items.en: Middle English dropped the initial h and wrote nekke, the shape that leads towards the modern spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语去掉了词首的 h，写作 nekke，这个形状一路通向现代拼写。

items.en: Modern English keeps neck for the body part and extends it to narrow parts of objects, the opening of clothes, a strip of land and an informal verb.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 neck 指身体部位，并扩展到物件细长处、衣服开口、狭长陆地，还多了一个口语动词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds in which the word survives; the near-meaning group collects neighbouring body and clothing terms.
note.cn: 形近组收仍保留这个词的复合词；近义组收相邻的身体部位与衣着用语。

normalIntro.en: One Old English body word, a lost h, and a habit of naming any narrow join after it: that is the whole history in brief.
normalIntro.cn: 一个古英语身体词、一个消失的 h，以及见到窄连接处就借用的习惯，就是这段历史的大概。

normal.en: Old English hnecca began with hn-, and Middle English simply dropped the h to give nekke.
normal.cn: 古英语 hnecca 以 hn- 开头，中古英语直接把 h 去掉，成了 nekke。

normal.en: Neckline and necklace are compounds that keep the body sense: the line and the jewellery both sit at the neck.
normal.cn: neckline 与 necklace 都是保留身体义的复合词：领口线和首饰都落在脖子处。

normal.en: A bottleneck borrows the shape, not the body: a bottle's narrow part holds traffic or work back.
normal.cn: bottleneck 借的是形状而不是身体：瓶子的细处把交通或工作卡住。

normal.en: Neck and neck pictures two horses whose heads are level, hence the meaning 'exactly equal'.
normal.cn: neck and neck 想像两匹马齐头并进，于是有了「不相上下」的意思。

normal.en: Break one's neck is violent in form but often means rushing dangerously fast.
normal.cn: break one's neck 字面很凶，实际常指拼命赶路、快得危险。

abstract.en: The neck is where a large head is balanced on a narrow support, which is why the word suits any risky narrow join.
abstract.cn: 脖子是让大脑袋架在窄支柱上的地方，所以这个词也适合任何危险的窄连接处。

abstract.en: A garment opening and a body part share one name because cloth is cut to follow the body it covers.
abstract.cn: 衣服开口与身体部位共用一个名字，因为布料是照着它所覆盖的身体裁出来的。

abstract.en: A neck of land is a place where two large worlds touch through a thin corridor.
abstract.cn: 地峡是两片大世界通过一条细走廊相接的地方。

senses.why: Old English neodian meant to have to have something; the verb keeps that plain sense of lack and requirement.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 neodian 意为必须有某物，动词保留了欠缺与必需的本义。

senses.example: The town has a need for more doctors.

senses.why: The verb became a noun naming the lack itself and what would fill it.

definition_zh: 邻居；邻人；邻近的人或物；毗邻
definition_en: a person who lives next door or close by; a person or thing standing beside another; and, as a verb, to be next to a place
core_image: 两家院墙之间只隔一道矮篱，篱上晾着同一根绳子上的衣物
scene: 楼道里的纸箱还没拆完，对门的人先端来一壶热水。The neighbour across the hall brought a kettle of hot water before the boxes were even opened.
sceneCN: 这里 neighbour 是「邻居」（第 1 个义项：住在近旁的人）；句意为纸箱还没打开，对门那位就端来一壶热水。图中可辨识物件：楼道、纸箱、水壶。

senses.title: A person who lives close by
senses.definition: someone who lives next door or very near to one's home
senses.definitionCN: 住在隔壁或离家很近的人
senses.example: Our neighbour upstairs plays the piano every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 楼上那位邻居每天傍晚弹钢琴。
senses.why: The Old English compound joins neah, near, with gebur, a dweller, so the word names the person who dwells near you rather than a friend or a relative.
senses.whyCN: 古英语复合词把 neah（近）与 gebur（居住者）拼在一起，字面上指的就是「住得近的人」，与朋友或亲戚无关。

senses.title: A person or thing placed beside another
senses.definition: the person sitting or standing beside you, or a thing lying next to another of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 坐在或站在你旁边的人，或与其他同类相邻的事物
senses.example: She leaned towards her neighbour at the table to hear the toast.
senses.exampleCN: 她凑向同桌的邻座，想听清祝酒词。
senses.why: Because the word marks only position, it can be used for a stranger in the next seat, and the same logic lets it describe a country lying beside another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词只标记位置，所以能用来指旁边座位上的陌生人，同样的逻辑也让它可以形容一个挨着另一个的国家。

senses.title: To stand next to a place
senses.definition: to be situated immediately beside or near a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 位于某处紧邻的位置
senses.example: The small farm neighbours a protected stretch of river.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小农场毗邻一段受保护的河道。
senses.why: Having named the dweller nearby, English turns the word into a verb for the dwelling itself standing beside another, which is a short step from a person to a place.
senses.whyCN: 既然已经指「住在近旁的人」，英语就把这个词改成动词，指房屋本身紧挨着另一处；从人到地点只差一小步。

intro.en: Neighbour is an Old English compound of two plain words, one meaning near and one meaning dweller. The British spelling keeps ou, and American English writes neighbor.
intro.cn: neighbour 是古英语里两个很朴素的词拼成的，一个表示「近」，一个表示「居住者」。英式拼写保留 ou，美式写作 neighbor。

items.en: The first element goes back to a reconstructed Germanic root for near, the same source as near and the archaic nigh.
items.cn: 第一个成分可上溯到日耳曼语中表示「近」的重构词根，与 near、古旧的 nigh 同源。

items.en: Neah meant near or close, and it survives as the first half of the compound neahgebur.
items.cn: neah 意为近、靠近，作为复合词 neahgebur 的前半保留下来。

items.en: Gebur meant a dweller or a fellow worker of the land, so neahgebur was the person living close by.
items.cn: gebur 指居住者或一同种地的人，所以 neahgebur 就是住得不远的人。

items.en: Middle English reshaped the word as neighebor, and the vowel and spelling shifted several times before settling.
items.cn: 中古英语把它改写成 neighebor，元音和拼写来回变过几次才固定下来。

items.en: Modern British English keeps neighbour with ou, while American English simplifies it to neighbor; the meaning and the history are the same.
items.cn: 现代英式英语保留带 ou 的 neighbour，美式简化为 neighbor；两者的含义与来历完全相同。

entries.definition: An older word for near, now mostly literary or dialectal.

entries.definition: A person who lives in a particular house or area, often used in compounds.

entries.definition: A person who lives in the area being talked about.
entries.definitionCN: 住在所谈地区的人；本地人。

normalIntro.en: The word is a compound of near and dweller, and the British spelling keeps an ou that American English drops.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由「近」与「居住者」复合而成，英式拼写保留一个美式会去掉的 ou。

normal.en: Neah means near and gebur means dweller, so a neighbour is simply the dweller nearest to you.
normal.cn: neah 意为近，gebur 意为居住者，所以邻居就是离你最近的居住者。

normal.en: The -bour part is the old word for a dweller, not the English word for a harbour, so do not read it as a port.
normal.cn: 拼写里的 -bour 是古语「居住者」，不是英语里表示港口的词，别把它读成码头。

normal.en: The verb use follows the noun, since a farm can neighbour a river: the word only marks what stands close.
normal.cn: 动词用法跟着名词走，农场可以 neighbour 一条河，因为这个词只标记「紧挨着」的位置。

normal.en: American English writes neighbor, and the shorter form follows the same pattern as harbor and color.
normal.cn: 美式写作 neighbor，缩短的拼写与 harbor、color 遵循同一规律。

normal.en: Next-door neighbour is the fixed phrase for the person in the house beside yours.
normal.cn: next-door neighbour 是固定说法，指紧挨着你家的那户人。

abstract.en: A word built from near and dweller turns geography into a relationship: closeness itself becomes a kind of company.
abstract.cn: 一个由「近」和「居住者」拼成的词，把地理变成关系：距离近本身就成了一种陪伴。

abstract.en: The British ou and the American missing u are the same word wearing two passports.
abstract.cn: 英式多写一个 u、美式省掉它，是同一个词拿着两本护照。

abstract.en: Calling a country a neighbour borrows the warmth of a doorstep for something as cold as a border.
abstract.cn: 把一个国家叫作 neighbour，是把门槛边的暖意借给了边界这样冰冷的东西。

examples.cn: 楼上那位邻居每天傍晚弹钢琴。

examples.en: She turned to her neighbour at the table and smiled.
examples.cn: 她转向同桌的邻座，笑了一下。

examples.en: The farm neighbours a stretch of protected river.
examples.cn: 这座农场毗邻一段受保护的河道。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the person who dwells near; from that, the meaning widens to anyone or anything beside you and then becomes a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「住得不远的人」；由此词义扩到身边任何人或物，最后又变成动词。

definition_zh: 街区；居住区；邻里；附近；大约
definition_en: the area around where someone lives; the people living there; and, in fixed phrases, nearness in place or a rough amount
core_image: 一排低矮的房子围出一个小广场，孩子在三轮车旁追跑
scene: 街角的小店把长桌搬到门外，各家端来自己做的菜。The whole neighbourhood turned out for the street party.
sceneCN: 这里 neighbourhood 是「街坊邻里」（第 2 个义项：住在这一带的人）；句意为整条街的街坊都出来参加街头聚会。图中可辨识物件：长桌、端菜的托盘、街角小店。

senses.title: The area around one's home
senses.definition: the part of a town where someone lives, together with the streets and buildings around their home
senses.definitionCN: 一个人居住的那一片城区，包括住宅周围的街道与建筑
senses.example: She knows every shop in the neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 这一带的每家店铺她都熟。
senses.why: The suffix -hood turns a neighbour into the state or range of neighbours, so the word starts as the zone marked out by people living near one another.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -hood 把 neighbour 变成「邻里所构成的状态或范围」，所以这个词最初就是由相互住得近的人划定的一片地带。

senses.title: The people who live in that area
senses.definition: the residents of such an area considered together as a community
senses.definitionCN: 把这一带的居民作为一个共同体来看
senses.example: The neighbourhood raised money for the new playground.
senses.exampleCN: 街坊们为建新游乐场凑了钱。
senses.why: Since the zone is named after the people inside it, the same word slides from the place to the people, a habit English often shows with words of community.
senses.whyCN: 既然这片地带是因住在里面的人而得名，同一个词就从地点滑到人身上，这是英语里表示共同体的词常见的走向。

senses.title: Nearness in place
senses.definition: the state of being close to a particular place, used in the fixed phrase in the neighbourhood of
senses.definitionCN: 靠近某一地点的状态，用于固定说法「在……附近」
senses.example: They bought a flat in the neighbourhood of the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站附近买了一套公寓。
senses.why: A neighbourhood is space around a point, so the word can serve in a purely spatial phrase that names no residents at all.
senses.whyCN: 街区本身就是某一点周围的空间，所以这个词能用在纯讲位置的短语里，完全不提住在那里的人。

senses.title: A rough amount or range
senses.definition: an approximate figure or amount, used in the phrase in the neighbourhood of
senses.definitionCN: 大致的数字或数量，用于短语「大约、上下」
senses.example: The repair will cost in the neighbourhood of three hundred pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修理大约要花三百英镑。
senses.why: Approximation is spatial nearness moved onto numbers: a figure close to the target is treated as the value living nearby.
senses.whyCN: 近似就是把空间上的「靠近」挪到数字上：接近目标的数字，被当成住在旁边的那个值。

intro.en: Neighbourhood is neighbour plus the old suffix -hood, the same ending that builds childhood and brotherhood.
intro.cn: neighbourhood 是 neighbour 加上古老的词尾 -hood，与 childhood、brotherhood 用的是同一个词尾。

items.en: The suffix had meant condition, state or rank, and it became -hood in modern English.
items.cn: 词尾 hād 意为状况、状态或身份，在现代英语里变成 -hood。

items.en: The base word named the person who dwells near, as a compound of near and dweller.
items.cn: 基础词由「近」与「居住者」复合，指住得不远的人。

items.en: Middle English formed neighbourhood for the state of being neighbours and for the district where they lived.
items.cn: 中古英语构成 neighbourhood，既指互为邻居的关系，也指他们居住的地段。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the word is common for a district of a town and for the people in it.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个词已常用来指城里的一片地段以及住在里面的人。

items.en: Modern British English keeps neighbourhood and American English writes neighborhood, while the fixed phrase in the neighbourhood of extends the word to nearness and rough amounts.
items.cn: 现代英式保留 neighbourhood，美式写作 neighborhood；固定短语 in the neighbourhood of 又把词义扩到「附近」和「大约」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built with the same -hood suffix; the near-meaning group gathers words for districts and their people.
note.cn: 形近组收用同一个 -hood 词尾构成的词；近义组收表示地段及其居民的词。

entries.definition: The period of life when a person is a child.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人身为孩子的时期；童年。

entries.definition: The relationship between brothers, or a group united by a shared cause.
entries.definitionCN: 兄弟之间的关系，或为共同事业联合起来的团体。

entries.definition: The state of being untrue, or a statement that is untrue.
entries.definitionCN: 虚假的状态，或一句不实的话。

entries.definition: A defined part of a town or country.
entries.definitionCN: 城镇或国家中划定的区域。

entries.definition: The area near a particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 某一地点附近的区域。

entries.definition: The people of a particular area considered together.
entries.definitionCN: 把某一地区的人作为一个整体来看的群体。

normalIntro.en: The word is neighbour plus -hood, and the suffix does the same work it does in childhood: it turns a person into a state or a stretch of life.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 neighbour 加 -hood，词尾的作用与在 childhood 里一样：把人变成一种状态或一段生活。

normal.en: The suffix -hood comes from an Old English word for condition, so neighbourhood is the condition or zone of being neighbours.
normal.cn: -hood 出自古英语中表示「状况」的词，所以 neighbourhood 就是「互为邻居」的状况或范围。

normal.en: Childhood, brotherhood and neighbourhood all use the same ending, which is why they look and feel alike.
normal.cn: childhood、brotherhood、neighbourhood 用的是同一个词尾，所以它们看上去、读起来都很像。

normal.en: American English writes neighborhood, dropping the u that British English keeps.
normal.cn: 美式写作 neighborhood，去掉了英式保留的 u。

normal.en: The phrase 「in the neighbourhood of」 works for both a place and a number, so it means near as well as about.
normal.cn: 短语「in the neighbourhood of」既能接地点又能接数字，所以既表示「附近」也表示「大约」。

normal.en: Neighbourhood watch is a real arrangement in which residents keep an eye on one another's homes.
normal.cn: neighbourhood watch 是真实存在的做法，居民互相照看彼此的房子。

abstract.en: Adding -hood to a person makes a place, a quiet reminder that streets are made of the people standing on them.
abstract.cn: 给一个人加上 -hood 就得到一个地方，这悄悄提醒人：街道是由站在上面的人组成的。

abstract.en: One word can mean a district, its residents and an approximate sum, because all three are measured from the same centre.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能指一片地段、住在里面的人以及一个大致的数目，因为三者都从同一个中心量起。

abstract.en: A word that turns nearness into a number shows how easily English moves from space to quantity.
abstract.cn: 一个把「靠近」变成数字的词，说明英语从空间滑到数量有多容易。

examples.en: The whole neighbourhood came out for the street party.
examples.cn: 整条街的街坊都出来参加街头聚会。

examples.en: She has lived in this neighbourhood for thirty years.
examples.cn: 她在这个街区住了三十年。

examples.en: The cost will be in the neighbourhood of two hundred pounds.
examples.cn: 费用大约两百英镑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「邻里护」——街坊互相护着，就有了邻里情；记住 neighbourhood 是街区、邻里。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是由相互住得近的人围出的地带；它分成地点、居民，以及表示邻近与约数的两个短语义。

senses.example: Neither of the two answers is correct.
senses.exampleCN: 两个答案都不对。
senses.why: The word is a contraction of the Old English phrase for not which of the two, so its whole job is to sweep both options away in a single gesture.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是古英语中「两者中的哪一个都不是」这一说法的缩合，所以它全部的活儿就是用一次动作把两个选项一起扫掉。

senses.title: Paired with nor to deny both
senses.definition: used with nor to connect two things that are both denied
senses.definitionCN: 与 nor 连用，连接两样都被否定的事物
senses.example: Neither the driver nor the passengers were hurt.
senses.exampleCN: 司机和乘客都没有受伤。
senses.why: Since the first half already denies both members of a pair, English repeats the denial with nor so that each item is explicitly ruled out.
senses.whyCN: 词的前半已经把一对中的两个都否定了，英语再用 nor 重复一次否定，让每一项都被明确排除。

senses.title: Also not, in agreement with a negative
senses.definition: used after a negative statement to say that the same is true of another person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用在否定句之后，表示另一个人或事物情况相同
senses.example: I cannot swim, and neither can my brother.
senses.exampleCN: 我不会游泳，我弟弟也不会。
senses.why: The denying force of the pronoun is reused as a short adverb, so a whole negative clause is compressed into one word plus a reversed subject and verb.
senses.whyCN: 代词里的否定力量被挪作简短副词，于是一整个否定从句被压缩成一个词加倒装的主语和动词。

intro.en: Neither is an Old English contraction of a phrase meaning not either, built from a negative word and the word for which of two.
intro.cn: neither 是古英语里「不是两者中的任何一个」这一说法的缩合，由一个否定词和表示「两者中哪一个」的词合成。

items.en: Na was the plain negative word, meaning no or not, and it supplied the first half of the compound.
items.cn: nā 是普通的否定词，意为「不、没有」，构成复合词的前半。

items.en: Hwaether meant which of the two, and it is the same word that became whether in modern English.
items.cn: hwæþer 意为「两者中的哪一个」，就是现代英语 whether 的来源。

items.en: Nahwther meant not either of the two, and in speech it was shortened to forms such as neither.
items.cn: nāhwæþer 意为「两者中哪一个都不是」，在口语中缩短成 neither 这类形式。

items.en: Middle English settled on spellings like neither, and the word worked both as a pronoun and as a conjunction.
items.cn: 中古英语固定为 neither 这类写法，这个词同时作代词和连词。

items.en: Modern English keeps it as the pronoun, in the paired construction with nor, and in the adverb use of short negative replies.
items.cn: 现代英语保留它作代词、作与 nor 搭配的配对结构，以及简短否定回答里的副词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the old element for which of two or merely the spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words of outright denial.
note.cn: 形近组收共享「两者中哪一个」这一古老成分的词，以及只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示彻底否定的词。

entries.definition: One or the other of two, the positive partner of this pair of words.
entries.definitionCN: 两者中的任意一个，是这对词里的肯定一方。

entries.definition: Lower or underneath, as in the old phrase the nether world; it only looks like neither, and the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 下面的、下方的，如旧说法「下界」；只是与 neither 拼写相近，词根不同。

entries.definition: Neither masculine nor feminine in grammar; the Latin word means neither, but it is not the English source.
entries.definitionCN: 语法上既非阳性也非阴性；拉丁语原词意为「两者都不」，但它不是英语这个词的来源。

entries.definition: Not one of any number, used for more than two as well as for two.
entries.definitionCN: 任何数量中一个也没有，既可用于两个，也可用于更多。

entries.definition: And not, used to continue a negative statement.
entries.definitionCN: 也不，用于延续一个否定说法。

entries.definition: No person at all, used of people rather than of things.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人也没有，用于人而不用于物。

normalIntro.en: The word is a contraction of not plus which of two, and that double denial is what every one of its uses carries.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「不」加上「两者中哪一个」的缩合，它每一种用法都带着这层双重否定。

normal.en: The first half is an old negative word, so neither always denies before it chooses.
normal.cn: 前半是一个古老的否定词，所以 neither 总是先否定，再谈选择。

normal.en: The second half is the same element that gives English whether, so the word is literally not whether of the two.
normal.cn: 后半就是给英语 whether 的那个成分，所以这个词字面是「两者中的哪一个都不」。

normal.en: Neither is followed by a singular verb in careful writing, because it denies each member separately.
normal.cn: 在严谨的写作里 neither 后接单数动词，因为它对每一个成员分别加以否定。

normal.en: The paired pattern needs nor, not or, since the second item is denied as well.
normal.cn: 配对结构要用 nor 而不是 or，因为第二项同样被否定。

normal.en: In short replies the word brings inversion, as in neither do I, which copies the order of a question.
normal.cn: 在简短回答里它会带来倒装，如 neither do I，照搬了疑问句的词序。

abstract.en: A word made of not plus which of two shows that a choice can be refused before it is even offered.
abstract.cn: 一个由「不」加「两者中哪一个」构成的词说明：选择可以在被提出之前就被拒绝。

abstract.en: Neither is the grammar of a closed door: two ways stand open, and both are declared shut.
abstract.cn: neither 是一扇关上的门的语法：两条路摆在面前，两条都被宣布关闭。

abstract.en: Its three jobs as pronoun, conjunction and adverb show how one small denial can hold a whole clause together.
abstract.cn: 它兼作代词、连词和副词，说明一个小小的否定能撑起整个从句。

examples.en: Neither of the two cups had been touched.
examples.cn: 两只杯子都没有被动过。

examples.en: Neither the driver nor the passengers were hurt.
examples.cn: 司机和乘客都没有受伤。

examples.en: I cannot swim, and neither can my brother.
examples.cn: 我不会游泳，我弟弟也不会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「你惹」——两个都惹了你，于是一个也不选；记住 neither 是两者都不。

root: 古英语 nā（不）加 hwæþer（两者中的哪一个）缩合为 nāhwæþer，后简作 neither；与 either、whether 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the denial of both members of a pair; it divides into the pronoun, the paired conjunction with nor and the adverb of agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是把一对中的两个一起否定；由此分出代词、与 nor 搭配的连词，以及表示「也不」的副词。

core.cn: 核心意象：两只杯子并排放着，两只都被推回原处，谁也没被端起。

branches.cn: 两只杯子被一起推回桌子中央

branches.cn: 一个人摇头，另一个人也跟着摇头

intro.cn: 这个词是两块古英语构件的缩合：一个否定词，一个表示「两者中哪一个」的成分；这两块构件至今解释着它的语法。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no reliable Latin cognate; its two parts are Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词；它的两个构件都来自古英语。

definition_zh: 紧张的；焦虑的；神经的；易激动的；神经质的
definition_en: anxious and easily worried; relating to the nerves of the body; highly strung and quick to react
core_image: 考场门口，一个女生反复整理袖口，眼睛盯着紧闭的门
scene: 考前的走廊里，一个女生站在门口，手指一遍遍捏着袖口，眼睛盯着紧闭的教室门。She felt nervous before the oral exam, so she kept checking her notes.
sceneCN: 这里是「紧张的、焦虑的」（第 1 个义项：面对考验时心里不安）；句意为口试之前她感到紧张，所以不停地看笔记。图中可辨识物件：走廊、袖口、教室门。

pos.zh: 紧张的；焦虑的；神经的；易激动的；神经质的

derivatives.zh: 由 nervous 加 -ly 构成，义为「紧张地；不安地」
由 nervous 加 -ness 构成，义为「紧张；神经质」
nervous 的词根，义为「神经；勇气」
由 nerve 加 -y 构成，义为「紧张不安的；有胆量的」

senses.title: Anxious and unable to relax
senses.definition: worried and unable to relax because something important or uncertain is about to happen
senses.definitionCN: 因为重要或不确定的事即将发生而担心、无法放松
senses.example: She felt nervous before the oral exam, so she kept checking her notes.
senses.exampleCN: 口试之前她感到紧张，所以不停地看笔记。
senses.why: The word born from sinews came to describe a body whose threads are pulled tight; English then read that tightness as worry, so a physical tension became the ordinary word for anxiety.
senses.whyCN: 这个从「筋」生出的词，后来形容身体里一根根线被拉紧的状态；英语又把这种紧绷读成担忧，于是身体的紧张成了日常表示焦虑的词。

senses.title: Relating to the nerves of the body
senses.definition: connected with the fibres and tissue that carry signals in the body
senses.definitionCN: 与体内传递信号的纤维和组织有关的
senses.example: Nervous tissue carries signals from the skin to the brain.
senses.exampleCN: 神经组织把信号从皮肤传到大脑。
senses.why: This sense is the oldest technical one, because the adjective was formed directly from the noun for a bodily cord; anatomy never lost the word, even after everyday speech took it over for worry.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项是最早的技术义，因为形容词直接由表示身体细索的名词构成；即使日常口语把这个词拿去表示担忧，解剖学也从未丢掉它。

senses.title: Highly strung and quick to react
senses.definition: easily excited or upset, reacting strongly to small things
senses.definitionCN: 容易兴奋或不安，对小事反应强烈
senses.example: The nervous dog hid under the table when the doorbell rang.
senses.exampleCN: 门铃一响，那只见人易惊的狗就躲到了桌子底下。
senses.why: An animal with fine, quick reactions is described as loosely strung rather than steady, so the same anatomical word moved from the wiring of the body to the temperament of a person or animal.
senses.whyCN: 反应细密而迅捷的动物，被形容为绳弦调得过松、不够稳当；于是同一个解剖词从身体的线路上，移到了人或动物的性情上。

intro.en: Nervous is the Latin adjective of sinew, which English first used for strong bodies and later for bodies whose nerves react too quickly.
intro.cn: nervous 是拉丁语中表示「筋」的形容词，英语先用它形容强壮的身体，后来才用它形容神经反应过快的人。

items.en: Nervus meant sinew, tendon or cord, the visible thread running through flesh and bone.
items.cn: nervus 意为筋、肌腱或细索，也就是穿过血肉与骨骼的可见细线。

items.en: Nervosus meant full of sinew, strong and vigorous, and it is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.cn: nervosus 意为多筋的、强壮的、有力的，是英语这个形容词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French nerveux kept the sense of strong and sinewy and passed the adjective into English with its spelling reshaped.
items.cn: 古法语 nerveux 保留「强壮、多筋」的意思，把形容词传入英语，拼写也做了改写。

items.en: English first praised nervous strength in bodies and writing; by the eighteenth century the word had moved to people whose nerves reacted too sharply.
items.cn: 英语最初用 nervous 称赞身体与文章中的强劲；到十八世纪，这个词转向形容神经反应过于敏锐的人。

items.en: Modern English keeps the anatomical sense beside the everyday one of worry, and applies the word to people, animals and situations alike.
items.cn: 现代英语把解剖义与日常的担忧义并排保留，并且把人、动物与处境都用这个词来形容。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the noun, adverb, abstract noun and informal adjective of the same family; the near-meaning group holds words for tension and low-level fear.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的名称、副词、抽象名词与口语形容词；近义组收表示紧绷与轻微恐惧的词。

entries.definition: The fibre itself, and also courage or boldness, the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 纤维本身，也指勇气或放肆，是形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: In an anxious manner, made by adding -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 以焦虑的方式；加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being anxious, made with -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 焦虑的状态；由 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: Anxious in British use, but bold in American use, made with -y.
entries.definitionCN: 英式指紧张不安，美式却指有胆量；由 -y 构成。

entries.definition: Worried about something uncertain, often with a sense of dread.
entries.definitionCN: 对不确定之事担忧，常带一点恐惧。

entries.definition: Tight and strained, used of muscles, situations and people alike.
entries.definitionCN: 绷紧、吃力的，可用于肌肉、局面与人。

entries.definition: Unable to keep still because of nerves, especially before an event.
entries.definitionCN: 因紧张而静不下来，尤指事情发生之前。

entries.definition: Slightly worried or uncomfortable, milder than nervous.
entries.definitionCN: 略有担忧或不舒服，语气比 nervous 轻。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of sinew, and its senses keep the same taut thread, read first as strength, then as sensitivity, then as worry.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「筋」的形容词，各义项保留同一根绷紧的线，先读作力量，再读作敏感，最后读作担忧。

normal.en: Nervous is built on nerve with the Latin ending -ous, so its literal shape is full of sinew.
normal.cn: nervous 由 nerve 加拉丁词尾 -ous 构成，字面形状就是「充满筋腱」。

normal.en: That literal sense praised strength, which is why older writing can call a vigorous style nervous.
normal.cn: 这个字面义曾用来称赞力量，所以较旧的文字会用 nervous 形容有劲的文风。

normal.en: The modern sense reversed the praise: a body whose nerves are too responsive is easily unsettled.
normal.cn: 现代义把这种称赞反了过来：神经反应过于灵敏的身体容易受扰。

normal.en: The anatomical sense survives in fixed phrases such as nervous system and nervous tissue.
normal.cn: 解剖义留在 nervous system、nervous tissue 这类固定搭配里。

normal.en: Nervously and nervousness simply add the manner and the state to the same adjective, so the family grows without a new root.
normal.cn: nervously 与 nervousness 只是给同一形容词加上方式与状态，词族因此不必另换词根。

abstract.en: A word for strong sinew becomes a word for fragile nerves, because the same thread can be praised as taut or blamed as over-sensitive.
abstract.cn: 一个指强健筋腱的词变成了指脆弱神经的词，因为同一根线既可以被赞为绷得紧，也可以被怪为过于敏感。

abstract.en: Standing before a closed door is the perfect picture of nervousness: the body is ready before it knows what will happen.
abstract.cn: 站在一扇关着的门前，是紧张最贴切的画面：身体在知道会发生什么之前就已经准备好了。

abstract.en: English lets one adjective cover the wiring of the body and the worry of the mind, which is how close the two have always been.
abstract.cn: 英语让一个形容词同时覆盖身体的线路与心里的担忧，可见这两者从来就很近。

examples.en: She gets nervous whenever she speaks in public.
examples.cn: 她每次当众讲话都会紧张。

examples.en: The nervous system controls how the body reacts.
examples.cn: 神经系统控制身体如何反应。

examples.en: He gave a nervous laugh and looked away.
examples.cn: 他局促地笑了一声，把目光移开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呢维斯」——神经像细线一样绷紧，人就坐立不安；nervous 就是紧张的。

root: 由 nerve（神经，源自拉丁语 nervus「筋」）加形容词词尾 -ous 构成；本义「多筋的、强壮的」，十八世纪起转指「神经敏感的、紧张的」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a taut cord; it yields the anatomical sense, the temperament of quick reactions, and the everyday feeling of anxiety.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一根绷紧的索；由此长出解剖义、反应迅捷的性情，以及日常的焦虑感。
